verses.zh: （ 可 拉 後 裔 的 訓 誨 詩 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 ） 神 啊 ， 我 的 心 切 慕 你 ， 如 鹿 切 慕 溪 水 。
verses.en: For the music director, a well-written song[NOTE:1] by the Korahites.As a deer[NOTE:2] longs[NOTE:3] for streams of water,so I long[NOTE:4] for you, O God!
notes: Psalm 42. The psalmist recalls how he once worshiped in the Lord’s temple, but laments that he is now oppressed by enemies in a foreign land. Some medieval Hebrew mss combine Psalms 42 and 43 into a single psalm.

The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.

Since the accompanying verb is feminine in form, the noun אָיִּל (ʾayyil, “male deer”) should be emended to אַיֶּלֶת (ʾayyelet, “female deer”). Haplography of the letter tav has occurred; note that the following verb begins with tav.
Or “pants [with thirst].”

verses.en: I cannot eat; I weep day and night.[NOTE:1] All day long they say to me,[NOTE:2] “Where is your God?”

verses.en: I will remember and weep.[NOTE:1] For I was once walking along with the great throng to the temple of God,shouting and giving thanks along with the crowd as we celebrated the holy festival.[NOTE:2]

verses.en: Why are you depressed,[NOTE:1] O my soul?[NOTE:2] Why are you upset?[NOTE:3] Wait[NOTE:4] for God!For I will again give thanksto my God for his saving intervention.[NOTE:5]

verses.en: I am depressed,[NOTE:1] so I will pray to you while in the region of the upper Jordan,[NOTE:2] from Hermon,[NOTE:3] from Mount Mizar.[NOTE:4]

verses.en: By day the Lord decrees his loyal love,[NOTE:1] and by night he gives me a song,[NOTE:2] a prayer[NOTE:3] to the God of my life.

verses.en: I will pray[NOTE:1] to God, my high ridge:[NOTE:2] “Why do you ignore[NOTE:3] me?Why must I walk around mourning[NOTE:4] because my enemies oppress me?”

verses.en: My enemies’ taunts cut me to the bone,[NOTE:1] as they say to me all day long, “Where is your God?”[NOTE:2]
